title: Personal brand and company brand
header_line: My analysis of one book on authority and personal brand. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Is your name your brand, or your company's?
A student said: trust in news and government organizations went down, and trust in individual reporters went up, because it was one person reporting the facts against giant conglomerates.

I said that the authority of the media outlets became fragmented in viewers' minds, and people began a search for information. I said that the author's thesis is that you cannot divorce the corporate brand from the personal brand.

I read a passage in which the strategy to build only one is based on two misguided notions, such as that an institution is more sustainable if not built on a person, and that building both a corporate brand and a leader's brand dilutes both. A student first heard it as a warning against doing both, and I read it again.

I said that you have to work on both: you as a person, a leader and the founder, with your credibility and trust, and the company and what gives it credibility. I used a famous founder and his company as an example of one that cannot be separated.
A student said: people did not care who the team was, they trusted her to choose the right people. You are the brand and people trust you.
What would people say your name stands for?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write what your name stands for.
Write what your company stands for.
Write what you will build for each.
Write who you would trust to choose a team for you.

check.q: What did I say the author's thesis is?
choices: You cannot divorce the corporate brand from the personal brand

check.q: What did I say became fragmented?
What did a student say about her team?
choices: People trusted her to choose the right people
People wanted to see every name
People did not care at all

recap: Work on both brands. People trust a person first.
